disputed: Whether Israel's conduct meets the legal definition of genocide (requiring proof of specific intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial, or religious group) is the central question before the ICJ and remains unresolved by any court. The UN Commission's finding, while significant, is not a judicial determination and is disputed by Israel and the US. Critics of US policy argue continued financial and diplomatic support despite the Commission's finding amounts to complicity; the US position is that no genocide has been proven to have occurred. On the UN vetoes: the US position is that any ceasefire text must condemn Hamas and require its disarmament, and that one-sided resolutions undercut US-led negotiations. Every other Security Council member, including US allies the UK and France, voted in favor both times.

items: As of September 2026, at least 73,400 people in Gaza have been killed, with roughly 10,000 more presumed buried under rubble, and at least 174,500 injured; the majority of victims are reported as civilians, and around half are women and children. (Wikipedia, citing UN/casualty tracking (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide))

Famine (IPC Phase 5) was confirmed in parts of Gaza in August 2025. Following an October 2025 ceasefire tied to a Trump administration peace plan, conditions improved somewhat, but as of late 2025, 1.6 million people still faced acute food insecurity, with over 100,000 in catastrophic conditions; most of Gaza was projected to remain in Emergency-level (IPC Phase 4) food insecurity through mid-2026. (ECCHR Q&A (https://www.ecchr.eu/fileadmin/Q_As/ECCHR_Q_A__Gaza_and_Genocide_20241210.pdf))
sections.label: Humanitarian and casualty data

items: The UN Human Rights Council's Independent International Commission of Inquiry concluded on September 16, 2025 that Israel is committing genocide, finding reasonable grounds that Israel had committed four of five genocidal acts defined under the 1948 Genocide Convention. (UNHRC Commission of Inquiry (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_UNHRC_Commission_of_Inquiry_report_on_Gaza_genocide))

South Africa brought a formal genocide case against Israel at the ICJ in December 2023. The ICJ has issued provisional (interim) measures in Jan/March/May 2024 ordering Israel to prevent genocidal acts and allow humanitarian access, but a final merits ruling on whether genocide occurred is not expected before 2026 at the earliest. (The Conversation (https://theconversation.com/is-israel-committing-genocide-in-gaza-international-court-will-take-years-to-decide-but-states-have-a-duty-to-act-now-263076))

The U.S. government - under both the Biden and Trump administrations - has consistently and explicitly rejected the genocide characterization, with State and Defense Department officials repeatedly stating they have seen 'no evidence' of genocide. Israel also rejects the characterization. (NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/defense-secretary-lloyd-austin-rejects-accusations-israel-committed-ge-rcna147031); Times of Israel (https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/us-state-department-rejects-un-report-accusing-israel-of-genocide-in-gaza/))

Other governments have taken a middle position, stating they are 'awaiting the ICJ verdict' rather than making an independent determination (e.g., Australia, Austria), reflecting a view that courts, not individual states, should resolve the legal question. (Wikipedia: Gaza genocide recognition (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_genocide_recognition))
sections.label: The genocide determination - contested

items: The U.S. has provided Israel more than $25 billion in support since October 2023. (Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/4/us-rejects-israeli-suggestions-of-removing-palestinians-from-gaza))

The U.S. has, at points, publicly broken with Israel on specific policies - for example, explicitly rejecting Israeli officials' calls in 2026 for depopulating/forcibly displacing Palestinians from Gaza, citing its own ceasefire plan's terms. (Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/4/us-rejects-israeli-suggestions-of-removing-palestinians-from-gaza))
sections.label: US financial and diplomatic support

items: June 4, 2025: the US was the lone 'no' in a 14-1 vote, vetoing a resolution that demanded an immediate, unconditional and permanent Gaza ceasefire, the release of all hostages, and the lifting of aid restrictions. Acting US Representative Dorothy Shea, a career diplomat, called it 'unacceptable for what it does say... [and] for what it does not say,' objecting that it did not condemn Hamas or call for its disarmament. (UN News (https://news.un.org/en/story/2025/06/1164056))

Sept 18, 2025: the US again vetoed a ceasefire resolution 14-1, its sixth Gaza ceasefire veto. It was cast by Morgan Ortagus, a political appointee. Ortagus said the text 'fails to condemn Hamas or recognise Israel's right to defend itself' and disputed the UN-backed famine finding as using 'flawed methodology.' (Al Jazeera (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/18/us-vetoes-un-security-council-demand-for-gaza-ceasefire-for-sixth-time))

Who Ortagus is: former Fox News contributor and State Department spokesperson under Pompeo (2019-2021). In 2022 she ran for Congress in Tennessee with Trump's endorsement but was removed from the ballot by the state party. She was Steve Witkoff's deputy Middle East envoy (Jan-June 2025) until moved out in an NSC purge of Israel and Iran staff, then became a senior policy adviser at the US Mission to the UN, a post that requires no Senate confirmation. She is close to Mike Waltz, who was confirmed as UN ambassador only days after the September veto. (Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_Ortagus); Jewish Insider (https://jewishinsider.com/2025/06/morgan-ortagus-u-s-mission-to-the-u-n-national-security-council/); NBC News (https://www.nbcnews.com/news/amp/rcna232480))
sections.label: Update - US vetoes at the UN Security Council (2025)

summary: Note on framing: whether Israel's conduct in Gaza legally constitutes genocide is a contested question before international courts, not a settled fact - this entry presents the documented data, the finding by one UN body, and the range of government positions, rather than adopting the label itself.
title: US policy toward Israel amid mounting genocide allegations in Gaza
